reviews.comment: Solid choice for Physical Organic Chemistry. The class itself is tough, but his lecture notes (always posted to Canvas) helped me prepare for the exams. Homework problems were creative and helped me grasp the material. Highly recommend.

I took Fang in the spring of 2020 when classes suddenly got pushed online. Dr. Fang did not make this transiton easy what so ever. He completly deviated from the syllabus and was constantly unsure about the format of exams, the final exam, and quizzes. He reads directly off the power point and gives few helpful examples. Try to take someone else.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Fang really knows about ochem, but this semester was wild. He is definitely not super friendly, & will sometimes get pretty annoyed when people ask questions. He randomly started giving us pop quizzes halfway through the semester & the homework was sometimes impossible. In the end though, he gave us a curve & I was happy with my final grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Fang is one of the best prof I've ever had at TAMU. He really wants his students to be successful and he tries his to help his students in any way he can. He does give pop quizzes in class so make sure you show up, homework are on owl and they can take some time to finish.

Really good professor. Lots of lecturing but overall is very clear on what he wants and how he wants you to do the problems. Go to SI, very helpful. He is available after class and genuinely cares for his students! He does not try to trick you on the exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great prof. is very clear on what he wants you to know for exams
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fang is a super cool prof. He genuinely want you to learn and won't try to make you fail like other ochem profs. You still have to work for it, but it is achievable. Do all you homework because its worth a test grade. Go to the SI simply for the review problems if you don't like the SI leader. But, they're usually pretty good at this level.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Fang is an amazing ochem professor. He is very clear in class and his tests are very straight forward. He is helpful in office hours and will explain whatever you need. GO TO SI. It helps SO much, because ochem is hard. You learn the material in this class, and it is also easy to make the grade you want. Great prof.
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had a great experience with Dr. Fang. He was very clear and concise with what he wanted you to learn and didn't waste time talking about other things that aren't related. His tests are tough with around a 65 average overall, but they aren't too bad if you pay attention in class and have a natural love for chemistry. He wasn't "inspirational".

Tests are straight forward, with a few tricky questions thrown in. He refuses to use power points (which I liked about him) so you have to be on your toes ready to take good notes. His notes and examples are directly from the textbook, so if you miss something he said, its easy to go back. He gets annoyed when people ask too many questions.
